content: 1. Participants and Roles: Mike Frick, representing the TB/HIV Project at the Treatment Action Group in New York, USA. Andrei Maryandyshev, Head of the Phthisiopulmonary Department in Arkhangelsk, Russian Federation. Nguyen Viet Nhung, Director of the National Lung Hospital and Manager of the Vietnam National TB Programme in Hanoi, Vietnam. Ejaz Qadeer, Ministry of Health, Islamabad, Pakistan. Abdul Hamid Salim, Advisor to the National TB Programme in Bangladesh, focusing on Global Fund and MDR-TB initiatives, based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Simon Schaaf, a pediatrician specializing in pediatrics and child health at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of Stellenbosch, South Africa. Holger Schünemann, Chair and Methodologist at McMaster University, Canada. Pedro Guillermo Suarez, affiliated with Management Sciences for Health in Arlington, VA, USA (unable to attend the meeting). 2. Guideline Development Group (GDG) and Evidence Review Group (ERG): Members of the GDG and ERG were required to submit WHO Declaration of Interest (DoI) forms to disclose any potential conflicts of interest, whether academic, financial, or otherwise. The WHO Guideline Steering Committee reviewed these declarations, along with curricula vitae, research interests, and activities, to ensure neutrality and independence. In cases where potential conflicts were identified, the WHO Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics Office was consulted for further clarification and advice. 3. Conflict of Interest Management: Individuals with significant declared interests were excluded from the GDG. ERG members also declared their interests, which were assessed for potential conflicts. Public notices were issued to allow external comments on any competing interests that may have been overlooked. 4. Declarations of No Interest: Several GDG members declared no interests conflicting with the guideline objectives, including Daniela Cirillo, Kelly Dooley (Co-Chair), Gustavo Do Valle Bastos, Raquel Duarte, Christopher Kuaban, Rafael Laniado-Laborin, Gary Maartens, Andrei Maryandyshev, Ignacio Monedero-Recuero, Maria Imelda Josefa Quelapio, Wipa Reechaipichitkul, Nancy Santesso (Co-Chair), Welile Sikhondze, and Armand Van Deun. 5. Non-Significant Interests: Five GDG members declared interests judged as non-significant, allowing their full participation. Examples include: Farhana Amanullah, who served as a pediatric TB expert for WHO missions and other grants. Tsira Chakhaiya, involved in TB Alliance clinical trials and community engagement projects. Michael Rich, employed by Partners in Health for work on clinical care guidelines and programmatic management of drug-resistant TB. Rada Savic, principal investigator for research grants on improving TB treatment options. 6. External Review Group (ERG) Declarations: ERG members such as Essam Elmoghazi, James Johnston, Enos Masini, Rohit Sarin, Kitty Van Weezebeek, Irina Vasilyeva, and Piret Viiklepp declared no interests related to the meeting objectives. Some ERG members were involved in unrelated clinical trials, which did not restrict their participation. 7. Specific Declarations: Charles L. Daley chaired data monitoring committees for delamanid and clofazimine studies, receiving compensation from pharmaceutical companies. Simon Schaaf received research support for pharmacokinetics work on second-line TB medicines in children. Helen Stagg received grants for consultancy work on MDR-TB clinical pathways and latent TB infection studies. Carlos A. Torres-Duque participated in national TB guideline updates in Colombia, providing evidence-based expert opinions without financial gain. 8. Independent Evidence Reviewers: Independent experts conducting systematic reviews for the guideline revision declared no interests related to the policy objectives. 9. Funding and Research Activities: Various members disclosed funding sources and research activities, such as grants from the NIH, Gates Foundation, and pharmaceutical companies. These were assessed for relevance and potential conflicts. 10. Technical Resource Participation: One GDG member, whose funding for new medicines for MDR-TB regimens was deemed a conflict, withdrew from the panel but participated as a technical resource. 11. Transparency and Public Engagement: The WHO ensured transparency by reviewing all declarations and inviting public comments to address any overlooked competing interests.
